title: SR-1.31 Every other CLI state writer goes through the daemon or the lock
request: Closes G96: SR-1.24 routes five CLI commands' state writes through the daemon, or the SR-1.01 vault lock when no daemon runs, and gates the daemon's state routes on a local request with the admin scope. Every other CLI process that writes vault state still writes it beside a live daemon: token revoke and rotate, devices enroll, remove and rotate, the cloud and relay commands, contracts on and off, deployment set, github setup, invite, memev init on an existing vault, license activate with a relay, the per-session hook and mcp processes when they mint a missing client token, the cli and doctor tokens that memev recall, card, claims, doctor and every bus subcommand reissue, the session-start hook's lead mark, onboarding and report, and the relay address command, which rewrites the relay's key file. Split from SR-1.24 at its three-round stop (lead decision under the owner's delegation, 31 October 2026): SR-1.24 keeps task 1; this contract takes SR-1.24's task 2 with round 3's answers about these writers, the token-mint route (a local request with the admin scope only) and the admin token's own rotation. Repository: memev. Depends on contracts: SR-1.24, SR-1.28, SR-1.01, QL-1.02. Sensitive path (tokens and the bus's routing files): the QL-1.03 checklist applies before merge.

tasks.title: Every other CLI state writer goes through the daemon or the lock
requirements: token revoke and rotate, devices enroll, remove and rotate, cloud on, off, use, funnel, url, connect, rotate-key and status --show-secrets, cloud relay on and off, contracts on and off, the contracts CLI's client token, deployment set, github setup, invite, memev init on an existing vault, and license activate when a relay is returned, make their change through SR-1.24's helper: in the daemon when it is present, under the SR-1.01 lock when it is not
an invite is minted and redeemed in the same process, the daemon when it is present, so a redemption never races a mint on invites.json and one code enrols one computer

the One writer paragraph of docs/DESIGN.md names every state file these commands and SR-1.24's five commands write: tokens.json, clients.json, config.json, devices.json, invites.json, tunnel-key.txt, relay.json and bus/

these commands decide presence and treat refusals exactly as SR-1.24's helper does (its presence and no-fallback requirements): no healthy() probe decides presence, and a 404 from an older daemon ends the command non-zero

the per-session processes, memev hook and memev mcp, get a missing client token from the daemon when it is present and never write tokens.json or clients.json themselves; with no daemon they mint it under the SR-1.01 lock; the hook still exits 0

every remaining CLI state writer, in src/cli/onboarding.mjs, src/cli/hooks.mjs, src/cli/mcp-stdio.mjs, src/cli/memory-cli.mjs, src/cli/doctor.mjs and src/cli/upgrade.mjs, goes through SR-1.24's helper, so the One writer paragraph is true of every CLI process
memev token rotate on the admin token's id rewrites .memev/admin.json with the new token, with no expiry, in the same daemon operation; memev token revoke refuses the only admin token with a message
license activate installs the licence and applies the relay default in one daemon operation, so a refusal or a timeout leaves neither half-applied

verifier.cmd: out=$(node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern='^T1-c19:' test/cli-one-writer-all.test.mjs 2>&1); rc=$?; printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -30; [ $rc -eq 0 ] && printf '%s\n' "$out" | awk -v pat='^T1-c19:' 'BEGIN { n = split(pat, alt, "|") } function flush(  i) { if (cand != "") for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (cand ~ alt[i]) hit[i] = 1; cand = "" } /^[[:space:]]*(not )?ok [0-9]+ - / { flush(); name = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]*(not )?ok [0-9]+ - /, "", name); if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*ok / && name !~ /# (SKIP|TODO)/ && name !~ /\.test\.m?js$/) cand = name; next } /^[[:space:]]*type: .suite./ { cand = "" } END { flush(); for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (!hit[i]) exit 1; exit 0 }'

criteria.statement: One full run of test/cli-one-writer-all.test.mjs passes every labelled subtest (T1-c17, T1-c18, T1-c19) with nothing skipped and nothing todo.

verifier.cmd: f=$(mktemp) && node --test --test-reporter=tap test/cli-one-writer-all.test.mjs >"$f"; rc=$?; [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && grep -Eq '^# skipped 0$' "$f" && grep -Eq '^# todo 0$' "$f" && awk -v pat='^T1-c17:|^T1-c18:|^T1-c19:' 'BEGIN { n = split(pat, alt, "|") } function flush(  i) { if (cand != "") for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (cand ~ alt[i]) hit[i] = 1; cand = "" } /^[[:space:]]*(not )?ok [0-9]+ - / { flush(); name = $0; sub(/^[[:space:]]*(not )?ok [0-9]+ - /, "", name); if ($0 ~ /^[[:space:]]*ok / && name !~ /# (SKIP|TODO)/ && name !~ /\.test\.m?js$/) cand = name; next } /^[[:space:]]*type: .suite./ { cand = "" } END { flush(); for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) if (!hit[i]) exit 1; exit 0 }' "$f"

criteria.statement: Changes stay in scope

stop_rules: If any criterion fails after the fix: STOP, report the measured result, the failing check and file:line. Do not start the next task.
If the work needs a path outside scope: STOP and ask the owner to amend the contract. Never widen scope silently.
